title: When do two circles on a base touch, miss or cross?
description: Two circles are drawn on a base of eight, with the two smaller lengths as radii, for three sets of lengths. The radii added together are compared with the base to tell whether the circles touch, miss or cross. Keeko doubts the touching case and says touching circles still make a triangle.
teaching_notes: One idea: compare the sum of the two radii with the base. Equal means touch, less means miss, and more means cross, and only crossing circles give a triangle. Watch for children who accept the touching case because the circles do meet.

source: On a base AB, take two circles whose radii are the two smaller lengths. For the sets 3, 5, 8 and 2, 5, 8 and 5, 6, 8 say whether the circles touch, miss or cross, and whether a triangle exists.
video_script.why: The child has seen circles on a base cross and now sees all three ways two circles can meet, and which of them give a triangle.
video_script.substitution: The base is the longest length, eight, and the radii are the two smaller lengths in each set.
video_script.anchor: A base of eight with two circles whose radii are the two smaller lengths
video_script.wrong_answer: touching circles still make a triangle
video_script.wrong_move: A child sees that touching circles do meet, takes the touching place as the third corner and calls it a triangle, though that place lies on the base.
video_script.payoff_line: A triangle exists only for the third set, where the circles cross.

final_answer.value: 3, 5, 8: touch, no triangle; 2, 5, 8: miss, no triangle; 5, 6, 8: cross, a triangle exists
final_answer.spoken: a triangle exists only for the third set, where the circles cross; in the first set the circles touch and in the second set they miss

never_show: the result for the third set before the answer beat
maths_rules: 3, 5, 8: radii 3 + 5 = 8 = base, circles touch at one place on the base, no triangle
5, 6, 8: radii 5 + 6 = 11 > 8, circles cross at two places, a triangle exists
the touching place lies on the base, so the three corners are in one line
video_script.design: One idea: compare the sum of the radii with the base. Three sets, three results; Keeko's doubt closes the video.

beats.on_screen: title card Touch, Miss or Cross?; a base AB with two circles; the sets 3, 5, 8 and 2, 5, 8 and 5, 6, 8

marks.ask: a base AB with two circles appears

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>On a base eigh B, draw two circles with the two smaller lengths as radii.
<bookmark mark='cases'/>Do the circles touch, miss or cross, and does a triangle exist?

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a base AB; a circle at A in blue and a circle at B in orange, with the two radii marked

marks.radii: the two smaller lengths are marked as radii at A and B

beats.colours: circle at A in blue, circle at B in orange
narration: <bookmark mark='base'/>The longest length, eight, is the base eigh B.
<bookmark mark='radii'/>The two smaller lengths are the radii of the circles at eigh and B.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the sets are three, five, eight; two, five, eight; and five, six, eight.

beats.on_screen: To find: how do the circles meet in each set, and is there a triangle?
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how the circles meet in each set, and whether a triangle exists.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: 3, 5, 8: radii 3 + 5 = 8, equal to the base; the circles touch

marks.sum1: 3 + 5 = 8 is written next to the base 8
marks.touch: the circles touch at one place on the base

narration: <bookmark mark='s1'/>Step one, take three, five and eight.
<bookmark mark='sum1'/>The radii add to three plus five, which is eight.
<bookmark mark='touch'/>That equals the base, so the circles touch at one place, and no triangle exists.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 2, 5, 8: radii 2 + 5 = 7, less than the base; the circles miss

marks.sum2: 2 + 5 = 7 is written next to the base 8
marks.miss: the circles are seen with a gap between them

narration: <bookmark mark='s2'/>Step two, take two, five and eight.
<bookmark mark='sum2'/>The radii add to two plus five, which is seven.
<bookmark mark='miss'/>Seven is less than the base, so the circles miss each other, and no triangle exists.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: 5, 6, 8: radii 5 + 6 = 11, more than the base; the circles overlap

marks.sum3: 5 + 6 = 11 is written next to the base 8

beats.colours: circle at A in blue, circle at B in orange
narration: <bookmark mark='s3'/>Step three, take five, six and eight.
<bookmark mark='sum3'/>The radii add to five plus six, which is eleven.
<bookmark mark='over'/>Eleven is more than the base, so the circles overlap and meet in two places.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: sum of radii = base: touch; sum < base: miss; sum > base: cross

marks.rule: the three cases are written in a list
marks.tri: a triangle label appears beside the last case

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step four, compare the sum of the radii with the base.
A sum equal to the base means touch, and a sum less than the base means miss.
<bookmark mark='tri'/>A sum more than the base means the circles cross, and only then is there a triangle.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 3, 5, 8: touch, no triangle; 2, 5, 8: miss, no triangle; 5, 6, 8: cross, a triangle exists
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>A triangle exists only for the third set, where the circles cross.
In the first set they touch, and in the second set they miss.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the touching circles
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: the touching circles with the touching place on the base AB glowing; a flat line through A, the place and B

marks.place: the touching place glows on the base AB

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks touching circles still make a triangle.
<bookmark mark='place'/>But the place where they touch lies on the base eigh B itself.
<bookmark mark='flat'/>A corner on the base puts all three corners in one line. That is flat, not a triangle.
